slides.title:
His first sale was
a *broken* laser
pointer.
slides.sub:
It sold for $14.83.
That is how eBay began 👇

slides.title:
Labor Day weekend.
Pierre Omidyar codes
*AuctionWeb* in a
spare bedroom.
slides.sub:
A side project on his personal site,
from his Silicon Valley town house
(TIME, Centre for Computing History).

slides.title:
To test his site, he lists
his $30 laser pointer.
It doesn't work, *even
with new batteries*.
slides.sub:
Starting price: $1.
No bids for a whole week (TIME).

slides.title:
Then a bidding war.
A stranger *wins it*.
slides.sub:
The buyer: Mark Fraser, a Canadian
(eBay Inc., Centre for Computing
History).

slides.title:
Omidyar writes to the
buyer: you know *it's
broken*, right?
slides.sub:
The reply: he collected broken
laser pointers. He knew exactly
what he was buying.

slides.title:
Strangers buying from
strangers. It works when
*the listing is honest*.
slides.sub:
His goal in 1996: "an open market
that encourages honest dealings"
(via Centre for Computing History).

slides.title: I believe that people are *generally good*.
slides.author:
Pierre Omidyar, eBay founder
(eBay Seller Summit 2015, via eBay Inc.)

slides.title:
Sept. 24, 1998: eBay goes
public at $18. It closes
day one at *$47.38*.
slides.sub:
850,000 users, up from 41,000
two years earlier (CNNfn).
All from a $1 listing.

slides.title:
Be honest.
It *sells*.
slides.sub:
The listing said "broken". It still sold.

✅ State flaws and limits clearly
✅ Real photos, not just perfect ones
✅ Show reviews, good and bad
✅ Clear shipping and return policy
